What’s more expensive: a high-speed rail line between London and Birmingham or Nasa’s recent manned mission to the moon?

HS2 was supposed to herald a new era for British transport, bringing it on par with low-cost, high-speed transport networks of the kind found in Japan and Germany. Instead, costs have spiralled, rail speeds have fallen and the competition date has been delayed.

Laurence Sleator, transport correspondent for The Times, tells us just how much cheaper per mile Nasa’s Artemis II mission was than HS2.
